To evaluate the performance of Mod-GCN in more specific cases than Erdős-Rényi graphs, we test it on the same graphs that were used as test inputs in [ 2 ] and compare its performance to that of the algorithms in [ 2 ] . The results are recorded in Figure 5 . Thankfully, Mod-GCN outperforms PI-GCN . Mod-GCN does not outperform PI-SAGE , but then again, we are presently more interested in exploring which design choices lead to improvements for the GCN algorithm than strictly outperforming the algorithms in [ 2 ] . In Section 4 , we show that PI-SAGE is actually beat by a relatively lightweight greedy algorithm. In this section, we introduce a lightweight greedy local search algorithm for approximate k k -coloring and demonstrate that recursive warm starts based on approximate ( k − 1 ) (k-1) -colorings lead to substantial performance improvements. We then show how this idea can be incorporated into the GNN-based approach, further boosting its effectiveness.
